Population and Employment Impacts
Projected Levels - Different assumptions and projections on labor force participation rates, Crow coal development levels, and the various Westmoreland production scenarios are necessary since there is no way of accurately predicting which set of conditions will prevail, or for that matter, whether any of them will prevail. The best approach is therefore to settle on a combination of conditions that is most probable, and then to attempt to establish some sort of confidence interval around the projections that are developed for this particular combination.
Because the labor force participation rates of Crows and non-Crow females in the study area differ appreciably from their national counterparts, it appears probable that these rates will rise toward the national averages as the employment opportunities in Big Horn County increase. It then follows that the converging participation rate (LFPR-2) is the more likely to occur.
Given the long lead-time required between mine planning and operations, the low level of Crow coal development (AF-1) is likely to prevail until at least 1980. After 1980, the moderate level of Crow coal development (AF-2) becomes increasingly more likely. The moderate development level (AF-2) assumes an eventual mining and shipment of 42 million tons of coal from nearby Crow coal resources other than Westmoreland's.
